problem: The CLI is a thin client that delegates all authorization to the server. It exposes ticket operations (create, rerun, continue, update-description) and goal operations (create with requireApproval flag, terminate, resume) but performs no client-side role or permission checks. Approval status is displayed but not enforced. The CLI is also packaged as a skill for AI agents (SKILL.md) — this skill content may need updates if MCP tool availability changes based on roles.

files.why: CLI ticket creation: POST /api/tickets. Parameters: title, description, repositoryIds, mode, afterTicketId, implementFromTicketId, referencedTicketIds. No client-side approval or role checks.
CLI ticket detail: displays approvalStatus when present (lines 76-78). Shows mergeQueueStatus. Read-only display.
CLI ticket listing: displays [APPROVAL_STATUS] tag (line 110). approvalStatus is in the response data structure.
CLI ticket update: PATCH /api/tickets/{id} with description only. No role checks.
CLI ticket rerun: POST /api/tickets/{id}/rerun. No approval or role checks.
CLI ticket continue: POST /api/tickets/{id}/rerun with continuationContext. Supports --dry-run.
CLI goal creation: POST /api/goals with requireApproval boolean parameter. When true, server transitions goal to PENDING_APPROVAL state before creating child tickets.
CLI goal detail: displays 'Approval Mode: enabled/disabled' based on requireApproval flag.
HTTP layer: hxFetch() with auth headers. API keys (hxi_) use X-API-Key header, others use Bearer. X-Helix-Org-ID header when orgId is present. Server errors surfaced to user.
Config management: HxConfig with apiKey, url, orgId. Multi-org support via ~/.hlx/config.json.
Skill definition for AI agents. Lists available CLI commands and guardrails. May need updates if MCP tool availability changes based on roles.
Detailed command reference with flags and usage patterns.
Scripts: build (tsc), typecheck (tsc --noEmit), test (node --test). Zero production deps — Node built-ins only.

facts: CLI performs zero client-side authorization or role checks — all enforcement delegated to server
CLI displays approval status from server responses but does not gate operations on it
Goal creation supports requireApproval flag — when true, goals transition to PENDING_APPROVAL before spawning child tickets
HTTP layer (hxFetch) surfaces server error responses (including 403s) directly to the user
CLI supports multi-org context via orgId in config — X-Helix-Org-ID header passed to server
API keys starting with hxi_ use X-API-Key header; other tokens use Bearer Authorization
CLI has no MCP server — it's a direct REST client that AI agents use via the skill framework
Skill content (SKILL.md + references/) defines how AI agents interact with the CLI
unknowns: Whether CLI skill content (SKILL.md) needs to document role-based restrictions or hard-blocked operations for AI agent awareness
